newsitem.title: PUERTO RICO: Piles of shoes, Yule decorations strewn by blast.
newsitem.headline: Piles of shoes, Yule decorations strewn by blast.

text.p: The working day had just begun on Thursday on Calle de Sandiego, a busy commercial street in San Juan's working class district of Rio Piedras.

The Humberto Vidal shoe shop had opened its doors on time at 8:30 a.m., and 19-year-old Karen Perez was among the staff waiting for the customers to arrive. Across the narrow street, children at the Collegio de la Milagro had just sat down for class.
Then a huge explosion rocked the morning calm.

"I thought it was an earthquake. The floor was shaking, everything was shaking," said Florita Arce, a secretary at the school that houses 500 students. "It was a horrible noise. All the windows shattered."
When she looked outside, "I saw smoke everywhere, clouds of smoke and dust," she said.

At least 20 people died in the blast, 62 others were injured and some 11 were missing in the rubble, according to officials. A search for victims was halted on Thursday evening when the remains of the six-story building became too unsteady for the safety of rescue workers.

Lourdes Perez maintained a worried vigil just outside the police barricade surrounding the building. Her daughter, Karen, had reported for work at the shop just before the blast and was among the missing.
"I've been waiting here since 9 a.m. this morning. I'll wait all night," she said, dabbing tears from her eyes.

Nuns wearing traditional habits rushed from the nearby Catholic school and church to help the injured after the explosion. Bodies of the dead were laid on the steps outside the church, and the nuns helped the injured to lay down on pews inside until ambulances arrived.
At the school, the 500 students aged 5 to 17 were unharmed.

"No one was hurt at the school, and our Virgin didn't suffer at all," Arce said, referring to a life-size statue of the Virgin Mary, a symbol of the school. In English, "La Milagrosa" means "the miracle."

The statue stood serene and intact in the courtyard -- surrounded by twisted metal, lumps of concrete and debris -- that overlooked the blasted-out shop. Piles of sandals, high-heeled shoes and other footwear were strewn throughout the neighborhood.

Scattered among the rubble were Christmas season items that had been on display in a gift shop next to the shoe store. A stuffed Santa Claus, a decorated Christmas stocking and other holiday decorations still bearing price tags lay among the rubble.
By nightfall, heavy equipment was brought in to scoop up debris, allowing engineers to erect braces in the collapsed structure. The search for survivors was to resume at dawn.
